title_en: Do You Have It in Chinese

sentences.en: It's raining in the afternoon, and my family doesn't have an umbrella.

t: is there or not; do you have
sentences.en: I go to a nearby store and ask the clerk: "Do you have umbrellas here?"
I go to the nearby supermarket again and ask: "Do you have umbrellas here?"
The supermarket clerk says: "Yes, this one is thirty yuan."
I pay, and carrying my new umbrella, I walk home.

vocab: is there or not; do you have

quiz.q: What does 有没有 do in a question?
a: Asks if something exists or is available

quiz.q: Where does the narrator go the first time to look for an umbrella?
What does the narrator do at the end of the story?
a: Waits for the rain to stop
Buys an umbrella and walks home

grammar.p: 有没有 + noun？（is there... or not?）
grammar.e: 有没有 puts 有 and 没有 back to back to ask a yes/no question about whether something exists or is available, without needing 吗.
grammar.x: 你们这儿有没有雨伞？— Do you have umbrellas here?

grammar.p: 有 + noun + 吗？（do you have...?）
grammar.e: Adding 吗 after 有 + noun is the more common, simpler way to ask if something is available.
grammar.x: 这儿有雨伞吗？— Do you have umbrellas here?

grammar.e: 又 marks a repeated action that has already happened, unlike 再 which is for an action not yet done.
grammar.x: 我又去了附近的超市。— I went to the nearby supermarket again.
